long_biography.plain_text:
Dzialga trained as an accountant at Canisius College before earning an MBA at Columbia Business School. He spent eight years at Goldman Sachs and rose to co-head of its technology merger group, then moved to General Atlantic in 1998. There he helped take the growth investor into new markets across Europe, Asia and Latin America and chaired its investment committee for a decade.

After leaving General Atlantic, Dzialga established Brighton Park Capital in 2019. The firm focuses on growth-stage software, healthcare and technology-enabled services, combining capital with operating support for founder-led companies. Its second fund closed with $1.8 billion of commitments. The Dzialga family also supports Duke's Women in Finance Initiative, a multi-year programme providing mentoring, technical training and professional access.
